questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the WHO Pandemic Agreement (PA) adopted in 2025. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Pandemic Agreement was adopted by the World Health Assembly exercising its treaty-making power under Article 19 of the WHO Constitution.
The Agreement enters into force only after ratification by every member-state of the WHO.
The Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) annex to the Agreement has already been finalised and ratified by member-states.
India voted against the adoption of the Pandemic Agreement at the World Health Assembly.
questions.explanation: Only statement 1 is correct: the WHA adopts conventions under Article 19 of the WHO Constitution. International treaties of this kind typically need ratification by a specified threshold of states (not all members) to enter into force, and the PABS annex is explicitly still under negotiation, not finalised. The article states no country voted against the PA; India was among the 124 adopting states.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: India's stakes in the Global Pandemic Agreement
questions.pyqLink: Tests WHO's constitutional treaty-making power and the ratification process for international conventions, akin to UPSC's recurring questions on WHO/IHR institutional structure.

questions.stem: With reference to the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) and the repo rate, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Monetary Policy Committee consists of six members, three from the RBI and three external members appointed by the Central Government.
The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against the collateral of government securities.
A revised repo rate takes effect for retail loans only after it is ratified by Parliament.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct and describe the statutory composition of the MPC under the RBI Act, 1934 (as amended) and the standard definition of the repo rate. Statement 3 is false — retail and small-business loans are automatically linked to an external benchmark (such as the repo rate) under RBI guidelines, and no parliamentary ratification is required for rate transmission.

questions.sourceTitle: RBI MPC speech: Weak monsoon, strong El Niño, rabi season, global crude prices - What Governor Sanjay Malhotra conveyed
questions.pyqLink: Tests the statutory framework of the MPC and repo-rate mechanics, a recurring static theme following UPSC 2022's monetary policy transmission question.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding India's foreign exchange reserves. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: India's foreign exchange reserves comprise Foreign Currency Assets, gold, Special Drawing Rights, and the Reserve Tranche Position in the IMF.
Special Drawing Rights (SDR) is a currency issued by the IMF that circulates alongside national currencies.
The Reserve Tranche Position represents the portion of India's IMF quota that India can draw upon without conditionality.
Foreign Currency Assets are held by the RBI exclusively in US dollars, so their reserve value never changes with movements in other currencies.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — these are the standard four components of reserves and the correct description of the Reserve Tranche Position. Statement 2 is wrong since the SDR is an international reserve asset/unit of account, not a circulating currency. Statement 4 is wrong because FCAs are held in multiple currencies and their dollar-value fluctuates with cross-currency movements, which is why reserves can fall even without intervention.

questions.stem: With reference to satellite communication services in India, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Satellite spectrum in India is assigned administratively rather than through auction, as provided under the Telecommunications Act, 2023.
A Global Mobile Personal Communications by Satellite (GMPCS) authorisation is granted by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI).
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the Telecommunications Act, 2023 lists satellite spectrum for administrative assignment rather than auction. Statement 2 is incorrect because, as the article notes, GMPCS authorisation is granted by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), not TRAI, which is only a recommendatory/regulatory body.

questions.stem: With reference to India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, which one of the following best describes a Data Fiduciary's obligation while processing the personal data of a child?
options: It must obtain verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian before processing a child's personal data, and is barred from undertaking tracking or behavioural monitoring of children.
It may process a child's data without consent if the purpose is stated to be educational or crisis counselling in nature.
It must obtain consent from the Data Protection Board of India instead of the parent before processing a child's personal data.
It is exempt from restrictions on targeted advertising directed at children if the platform carries a visible age-disclaimer.
questions.explanation: The DPDP Act, 2023 requires Data Fiduciaries to obtain verifiable parental/guardian consent before processing a child's data and specifically prohibits tracking, behavioural monitoring, and targeted advertising directed at children. The other options describe obligations or exemptions that do not exist under the Act — the Data Protection Board is an adjudicatory body, not a consent-granting authority, and there is no blanket educational/counselling carve-out or age-disclaimer exemption.

questions.stem: Statement-I: The Election Commission of India can undertake a Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in any State. Statement-II: Article 324 of the Constitution vests in the Election Commission the power of superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are factually correct, and Statement-II is the correct explanation: the ECI's authority to order a Special Intensive Revision of rolls (as seen in the Karnataka controversy) flows directly from its Article 324 power of superintendence, direction and control over roll preparation, read with the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

Pair 3 is wrong — Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres are implemented under the National Health Mission by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, not the Ministry of Rural Development.

questions.stem: In the context of the ongoing controversy over the Chief Election Commissioner's conduct, consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: The Chief Election Commissioner of India is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a Selection Committee comprising the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

Statement-II: This selection mechanism is laid down in the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which governs the appointment process in place of any role for the Chief Justice of India.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: The 2023 Act created a three-member Selection Committee of the PM, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM, and the Leader of Opposition, replacing the Supreme Court's 2023 interim arrangement that had included the CJI. Statement-II correctly states the legal basis and explains why the composition in Statement-I holds, so both are correct and II explains I.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding India's construction and cement sector emissions in the context of its net-zero commitment:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: India has set a target to become a net-zero emissions economy by 2070.
The construction sector, which consumes steel and cement, contributes about 35% to 40% of global greenhouse gas emissions.
The cement sector's share of global emissions (7% to 11%) is lower than the share contributed by the global aviation sector.
Portland cement, the standard binding agent used in modern construction, was developed in Britain in the 19th century.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: India's net-zero target of 2070 was announced at COP26; construction contributes 35-40% of global GHG emissions; and Portland cement was developed in Britain in the 1820s. Statement 3 is incorrect — cement's 7-11% emission share is almost double that of aviation, not lower.

questions.stem: With reference to malaria, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Malaria is caused by a parasite of the genus Plasmodium, transmitted through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.
'Indigenous' malaria cases refer to infections acquired through local transmission within a region, while 'imported' cases are acquired outside that region.
The National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct and factually standard (the article itself defines indigenous versus imported transmission). Statement 3 is incorrect — the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme functions under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, not MoEFCC.

questions.stem: With reference to the Indian Air Force, which one of the following best describes its institutional origin and evolution?
options: It was established on 8 October 1932 as the Royal Indian Air Force, with the prefix 'Royal' dropped after India became a Republic in 1950.
It was established in 1947 immediately after independence as a wholly new service distinct from any pre-independence air arm.
It was established in 1932 as a wing of the Indian Army and became a separate service only after the 1962 war with China.
It was established on 8 October 1950, the day commemorated today as Air Force Day.
questions.explanation: The Indian Air Force was raised on 8 October 1932 as the Royal Indian Air Force; the 'Royal' prefix was dropped when India became a Republic in 1950, but the founding date of 8 October 1932 is what Air Force Day commemorates. The other options misstate the founding year, the service's continuity, or conflate the Republic Day of the IAF's renaming with its establishment.

questions.stem: With reference to the El Niño phenomenon, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: El Niño refers to the anomalous warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, off the coast of Peru and Ecuador.
El Niño events typically recur every two to seven years and are generally associated with below-normal rainfall during the Indian southwest monsoon.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. El Niño is the periodic warming of Pacific surface waters off South America, recurring every two to seven years, and is a well-established static syllabus link to weak Indian monsoon years, which the article references as a factor behind an unusually warm 'super' El Niño this year.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the conservation status of the Asian elephant in India:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Asian elephant is listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, which accords it the highest degree of legal protection.
The Asian elephant has been declared India's National Heritage Animal.
Project Elephant is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 1992 under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
The Synchronised All India Elephant Census is conducted by the Ministry of Home Affairs once every five years.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the Asian elephant has Schedule I status, was declared National Heritage Animal in 2010, and Project Elephant (1992) is run by MoEFCC. Statement 4 is incorrect — the elephant census is conducted by MoEFCC and State Forest Departments, not the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.sourceTitle: GPS study on elephant movements aims to mitigate conflicts in Assam

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the cheetah reintroduction effort in India, in the context of the recent release of cheetahs in Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve, Madhya Pradesh. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The cheetah was officially declared extinct in India in 1952.
Project Cheetah involved translocation of cheetahs from Namibia and South Africa.
The cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) is listed as 'Critically Endangered' on the IUCN Red List.
Kuno National Park, one of the cheetah's habitats under the project, is located in Madhya Pradesh.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are factually correct — the cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952, Project Cheetah brought founder cheetahs from Namibia (2022) and South Africa (2023), and Kuno National Park lies in Sheopur district, Madhya Pradesh. Statement 3 is false: the cheetah's global IUCN status is 'Vulnerable', not 'Critically Endangered' — a near-miss distractor with categories like the Great Indian Bustard, which genuinely is Critically Endangered.

questions.stem: With reference to the Reserve Bank of India's Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against eligible collateral.
The Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate is normally kept lower than the repo rate.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — repo is RBI's instrument to lend against government securities as collateral. Statement 2 is incorrect: the MSF rate is a penal, emergency-borrowing rate kept above the repo rate, confirmed by the October 2026 revision where MSF stood at 5.75% against a repo rate of 5.50%.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: All recommendations of the GST Council are legally binding on both the Union and State Governments.
The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A of the Constitution of India.
The Union Finance Minister serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of the GST Council.
questions.explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct — the GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A, chaired ex-officio by the Union Finance Minister. Statement 1 is incorrect: in Union of India v. Mohit Minerals (2022), the Supreme Court held that GST Council recommendations have only persuasive value and are not strictly binding on the Centre or States.

questions.stem: With reference to the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Violation of FEMA provisions is primarily a criminal offence attracting mandatory imprisonment.
FEMA is administered by the Reserve Bank of India and regulates cross-border trade and foreign exchange transactions.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct — FEMA, 1999 is RBI-administered legislation governing current and capital account forex transactions, as reflected in RBI's recent clarifications on reporting requirements for exporters. Statement 1 is incorrect: unlike the erstwhile FERA (a criminal law), FEMA treats violations as civil offences, enforced through monetary penalties and adjudication, not mandatory imprisonment.

questions.stem: With reference to recent RBI commentary on UPI transactions, which one of the following best describes the term 'Merchant Discount Rate (MDR)'?
options: MDR is the minimum cash reserve ratio merchants must maintain with their bank.
MDR is the interest-rate spread between the repo and reverse repo rates.
MDR is the discount RBI offers to merchant establishments on bulk cash deposits.
MDR is the fee merchants pay their bank or payment aggregator for processing digital or card payment transactions.
questions.explanation: MDR is the fee charged to a merchant by their bank or payment service provider for enabling digital payment acceptance, usually a percentage of transaction value — the subject of RBI's recent decision to permit a 0.4% MDR on UPI transactions above ₹2,000. The other options invent unrelated banking concepts (CRR, interest-rate spreads, cash-deposit discounts) that do not describe MDR.
